title: Contradiction Lens — quickscore & handoff
content:
Purpose: rapid, defensible pass/hold/pass+condition recommendation after panel. This is my scratchpad to capture contradictions and uncertainties before the formal debrief. Keep it short — things we can act on or follow up.

Context: Senior Runtime Engineer loop (onsite simulated). Two small pair tasks, a system design sketch, and 30m behavioral. Panel = 4 interviewers (infra, runtime, sre, product). Candidate: senior IC, background at infra-adj company, strong latency-tuning examples but lighter on deployment automation.

Quickscore rubric (0–3 each):
- Systems mental model: 2 (good infra mental model, missed a few edgecases on KV cache invalidation)
- Runtime internals: 3 (explained KV caching, attention cache tradeoffs clearly)
- Coding: 1 (pairing felt slow, small bugs, but logic OK)
- Debugging: 2 (reasonable approach but missed root-cause in one probe)
- Production operability: 1 (thin on autoscaling and rollout policies)
- Communication & tradeoffs: 2 (clear, but sometimes anchored on single solution)

Score total: 11/18 — leans hire-ish but with operational gaps.

Green signals (what stood out):
- Concrete micro-optimizations described (KV sharding, prefetched KV caching) with empirical tradeoffs and when to avoid them.
- Strong intuition about memory-pressure vs throughput in multi-tenant GPU pools.
- Thoughtful about graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model family when GC spikes.

Red flags / contradictions to resolve:
- Claims to have implemented autoscaler in previous role but code examples were high-level; asked for repo links and got only internal docs. Follow-up: ask for PR or design doc.
- Candidate insists they prefer single-language infra (Go-only) but current team is polyglot (Python + Rust + Go); need concrete examples of cross-language collaboration.
- Slow on whiteboard coding: either nerves or gap in algorithmic fluency. Panel difference: infra interviewer scored 3 on coding; runtime interviewer scored 1. (Annotate differences: infra liked architecture narrative; runtime expected idiomatic patterns.)

Unresolved questions to surface in calibration / reference check:
- Did they own an autoscaling rollout end-to-end? Which metrics drove scale decisions?
- How do they write deploy-once, rollback-fast runbooks? Any incident postmortem authored?
- Specific PRs to read: ask recruiting to pull GH links for the Autoscale/Telemetry components they mentioned.

Proposed hire conditions (if hired):
- Ramp focus areas first 3 months: (1) deploy/runbooks + canary/rollback flows; (2) autoscaling policy tests + load harness improvements; (3) pair with runtime for coding patterns.
- Mentorship: pair with an SRE and runtime engineer for first 8 weeks.
- Short-term goal: deliver a canary-to-production runbook and a small autoscaling test harness.

Recommendation (quick): HOLD -> recommend in-depth take-home or 1-week paid trial to validate coding & operational ownership. Rationale: deep systems thinking present, but operational execution evidence is mixed.

Handoff checklist for recruiter / hiring manager:
- Request: candidate GH/PR links for the two autoscaling projects they referenced.
- Ask references about end-to-end ownership and incident narratives.
- If we move forward: propose a 4-hour paid trial (1.5h coding + 1h design + 1h ops simulation + 0.5h debrief).

Notes-to-self / follow-up items:
- Add a short paragraph in the panel sync about disagreement in coding score and ask panelists to cite specific lines or moments.
- Send candidate a thanks note with outline of potential next steps and transparency about concerns.
- If references check out strongly on ops, update score and recommend hire.

Raw snippets from panel: (copied in freeform)
- "They described a KV cache invalidation that relies on TTL only; I'd prefer explicit invalidation hooks for model version rollouts." — SRE
- "Good examples of memory-first optimizations; would pair well on kernel tuning." — Runtime
- "Pairing felt slow; had trouble with basic list manipulation under time pressure." — Infra

Tone for debrief: balanced. Call out concrete evidence for each score. Avoid gut-only language. If we land on a paid trial, define acceptance criteria up-front (tests, runbook, PR quality).

End.
